paper_of_week.headline: ReLU Networks’ Closure Revealed: Surprising Gaps in Function Space
paper_of_week.summary: The authors prove that the class of single‑hidden‑layer ReLU networks with a bounded number of neurons is weakly closed in Sobolev spaces, settling a long‑standing question about the topological properties of neural function classes. Their analysis leverages compactness arguments and explicit construction of counterexamples to demonstrate when closure fails under relaxed constraints. The work clarifies the theoretical limits of representational capacity and informs regularization strategies for deep learning practitioners. By pinpointing the exact conditions under which the set is or isn’t closed, the paper provides a rigorous foundation for future work on network approximation and optimization landscapes.
paper_of_week.key_takeaway: When designing architectures, enforce neuron count limits to retain closedness and avoid pathological convergence.

paper.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
paper.summary: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

deep_dive.problem: Understanding the topological closure of ReLU network function classes is essential for guarantees about convergence of training algorithms and the existence of limit points. Prior work left ambiguous whether limiting sequences of bounded‑size networks remain representable within the same class, especially in weak Sobolev topologies relevant to PDE‑inspired learning. This uncertainty hampers theoretical analysis of over‑parameterization and generalization.
deep_dive.approach: The authors fix a domain Ω⊂ℝ^d and consider the set N_N of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most N neurons. They embed these functions in the Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Ω) and prove weak closure by showing any bounded sequence admits a subsequence converging to a function that can be expressed as a ReLU network with ≤N neurons, using a diagonal argument on the affine parameters. To demonstrate non‑closedness under relaxed conditions (e.g., allowing unbounded weights or deeper architectures), they construct explicit sequences whose limits are piecewise linear functions that cannot be realized with the original neuron budget, thereby providing a counterexample.
deep_dive.results: The main theorem states: N_N is weakly closed in W^{1,p}(Ω) for any 1≤p<∞. Empirically, they validate the theorem by training shallow ReLU nets on synthetic piecewise linear targets and observing convergence to functions still representable within the neuron budget. Conversely, when they remove the neuron bound, they exhibit divergence to functions with finer kink structures, confirming the theoretical non‑closedness. Quantitatively, the Sobolev norm of the residual between the limit function and the best N‑neuron approximation remains >0, illustrating the gap.
deep_dive.limitations: The analysis is restricted to single‑hidden‑layer networks; extending to deeper ReLU architectures remains open and may exhibit different closure behavior. The weak topology considered does not capture pointwise or uniform convergence, so practical training dynamics (often governed by stronger norms) might not align with the theoretical guarantees. Moreover, the results assume exact arithmetic; numerical precision could affect the observed closure in real implementations.
deep_dive.what_it_unlocks: Practitioners can now design model selection pipelines that enforce explicit neuron caps to guarantee that training trajectories stay within a closed function class, simplifying convergence diagnostics. It also enables the development of regularizers that penalize excursions toward non‑closed regions, improving stability in low‑resource settings. Finally, the theoretical framework can be adapted to certify that certain network pruning strategies preserve representational closure.

one_thing_to_try.action: Train a 1‑hidden‑layer ReLU net with a fixed neuron budget and monitor Sobolev‑norm convergence.
one_thing_to_try.why: It directly tests the paper’s closure claim on your own data.
